parts.text:
"Use only the configured Fantasy Asset Forge MCP tools and the supplied workflow instructions. Do not read or search project files, run shell commands, construct canonical asset JSON, edit source, post-process images or GLBs, or use network tools.

Build and verify the committed Ranger reference loadout on a fresh adventurer: a spear in the main hand, leather armor on the body, a quiver on the back, and a belt pouch at the waist. First inspect the exact runtime capabilities needed for the adventurer reference, accessory discovery and task operations, immutable revision comparison, static idle/action poses, directional sprites/contact sheets, and GLB. Create the adventurer reference and record the baseline revision. Inspect its overview plus complete bounded parts, connections, poses, variants, and renderProfiles pages. Use archetypeId \"ranger\" for loadout discovery. Plan the entire loadout through search_accessories and inspect_template. Use only response-derived candidate identities, occupied part IDs, exampleOperation payloads, materials, placements, orientation guidance, required feature contracts, and visual checks. Never invent a transform, quaternion, port, connection, part ID, material, or canonical patch.

Remove any initial equipment that is not part of the requested loadout by using only occupied part IDs returned by public inspection or discovery, with exact dry-run/apply replay. For each requested Ranger accessory, dry-run the selected candidate's complete returned exampleOperation, inspect its returned affected/removed/added IDs and change preview, then replay the same request with only dryRun changed to false against the same expected revision. Re-inspect the complete parts and renderProfiles pages after equipping. Compare the baseline to the equipped idle revision. Validate, render all eight directional sprites and the contact sheet, and export GLB for that equipped idle revision.

Then dry-run and apply the declared action pose using the current revision, render and export the equipped action revision, and compare idle to action. Finally unequip every Ranger accessory using only the exact equipped part IDs returned by the public operation responses; use exact dry-run/apply pairs, render the action-pose unequipped revision, and compare the equipped action revision to the unequipped revision. Stop on any tool envelope with ok false or any unexpected affected ID.

Report: chronological revision lineage; every public tool call in order; each exact dry-run/apply pair and whether the inputs were identical except for dryRun; affected, added, removed, connection, and preserved IDs; validation bounds and triangle budget; returned render/contact-sheet/frame and GLB/manifest paths for equipped idle and action revisions; required-feature metrics and any failing direction; retries/corrections; limitations; and a final pass/partial/fail verdict. You cannot visually open the interactive 3D inspector, contact sheet, native 128x128 PNGs, or load the GLB with the allowed tool set, so mark those direct visual/importer surfaces Not Assessed rather than claiming them from metrics or paths. Temporal animation, atlases, cloth physics, gameplay inventory, novel identity/anatomy, Unity, Godot, and gameplay-runtime import are outside scope and must remain unsupported or Not Assessed according to runtime capabilities.
"
